sentences.text: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurine measuring about five meters in length and reaching a mass of up to 1.9 metric tons.
When fully grown it attained a total length of five meters, a size comparable to a large bus.
Adult skulls measured roughly thirty centimeters long, providing a broad platform for its beak and armor.
Most postcranial material belongs to juveniles, with the holotype of P. mephistocephalus measuring just under three meters.
Weight estimates vary, with Gregory S. Paul suggesting around 1.9 tons and Thomas R. Holtz proposing a range between 454 and 907 kilograms.
A fossilized larynx from a juvenile specimen indicates the animal could produce loud, possibly bird-like calls.
Unlike many ankylosaurs that are found on their backs, Pinacosaurus juveniles are commonly discovered lying on their stomachs with legs tucked inward.
Its tail ended in a heavy club that could be swung actively to deter predators.
The genus name derives from the Greek word for “plank,” a reference to the small rectangular armor plates on its head.
The type locality for Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum lies within the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia.
The species was formally named by Penkalski in 2026.
The first Pinacosaurus remains were uncovered in 1923, and the type species P. grangeri was described by Gilmore in 1933.
The holotype was recovered from a layer of the Djadokhta Formation that dates to the Campanian stage.
Pinacosaurus employed a smooth beak to clip low-growing vegetation, which was then sliced by small teeth and processed in an enormous hind gut.
Its small, slowly replacing teeth suggest reliance on a muscular tongue and associated tongue bones for food manipulation.
Researchers infer it ate tough leaves and pulpy fruits while avoiding fibrous stems and pine needles.
It likely favored soft, low-lying ferns that were easy to cut and digest.
During growth, ribs began to fuse with vertebrae, and the forelimbs became robust enough to bear most of the body’s weight.
The forelimbs grew disproportionately larger than the hind limbs, indicating the arms supported the majority of the animal’s mass.
Its relatively light build may have enabled it to confront small theropods such as Velociraptor, striking with its tail club.
Large theropods are absent from its ecosystem, though smaller predators like Velociraptor were present.
Juvenile groups appear to have moved together in herds that were suddenly buried by sandstorms, preserving them in a resting pose.
The genus itself was established by Gilmore in 1933.
Maleev’s Syrmosaurus viminicaudus, named in 1952, is currently regarded as a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
In 2026 Penkalski reassigned P. mephistocephalus to the separate genus Eopinacosaurus based on distinct skull and cranial armor features.
Pinacosaurus inhabited Mongolia and China during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago.
Its environment was a semi-desert landscape dotted with oasis-like water sources.
Arbour and Currie (2015) argued that Heishansaurus pachycephalus is a nomen dubium, questioning its validity as a distinct species.
Some researchers have proposed that Pinacosaurus may have exhibited ant-eater-like insectivorous behavior, a hypothesis that remains contested.
The precise function of the nasal opening arrangement in Pinacosaurus is still unclear.
Gregory S. Paul (2010) suggested that P. mephistopheles could be a junior synonym of P. grangeri, a view that has not reached consensus.
